editorial:
Imagine feeling like a ghost in your own home, ignored by everyone while your sibling gets all the love. That is exactly where you find Masako. She is shy and awkward, but inside, she is boiling over with anger. When she finally snaps and kills her sister, her life turns into a wild ride of running away and trying to hide. The vibe is a strange mix of a sad family drama and a dark crime story. You will feel for her loneliness, but you will also be shocked by how fast things spiral out of control.

The acting is the best part because you really see the change in Masako as she learns to survive on her own. The pacing is steady, though some parts feel a bit slow until the chaos kicks in. If you like stories about people hitting rock bottom and changing their identity, you will love this. Since it is an older film, you should look for a 4K Blu-ray to add to your physical collection for the best picture. Otherwise, renting it on Apple TV is a great way to see it without spending too much.
endingExplained: In the end, Masako tries to escape her past by changing her face through surgery. She hopes a new look will give her a fresh start and erase her guilt. However, she realizes that changing her outside doesn't fix the pain inside. The movie wraps up by showing that you cannot run away from who you are. She eventually has to face the truth about her crime and herself, showing that true change comes from within.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dark character studies and crime dramas.
